appStore.summary: Impressions, product page views and Get taps come from Apple's App Store Discovery and Engagement report through the App Store Connect key connected in Integrations. Conversion is Get taps divided by unique impressions.
appStore.detail: Apple drops rows under five users and adds small noise, and a day is final three days later. Totals add unique counts across markets and sources, so they read slightly high.

googlePlay.summary: Store listing visitors and acquisitions come from the monthly store performance files Play Console writes to its Cloud Storage bucket, read through the Google Play connection in Integrations. Conversion is acquisitions divided by visitors.
googlePlay.detail: A market reads the country file and All markets the traffic source file, so the two split sources differently. Google posts a day three to seven days later and changed how it counts visitors and acquisitions on July 10, 2026, so compare periods on the same side of that date.

appStore.freshness: Apple finishes a day within three days; the newest days may still grow.

ratingsByMarket.title: Ratings by market
ratingsByMarket.caption: Rating and number of ratings on the newest listing captured in each market
ratingsByMarket.onlyOneBody: The App Store keeps a rating for each storefront. Track a keyword in another market and the daily run captures the listing there, so its rating appears next to this one.
ratingsByMarket.helpTitle: How ratings by market are read
ratingsByMarket.helpSummary: The App Store keeps a separate rating for each storefront. Each row is the average and the number of ratings on the newest listing {product} captured in that market.
ratingsByMarket.helpDetail: The last row averages the markets above it, each weighted by its number of ratings. It covers only the markets listed here, not every storefront, and each market was captured on the day in its last column.
